why: The full .NET mutation run, split so its shards can run in parallel and be rerun one at a time. On a 4-core hosted runner the shards that finished took 50 minutes to 2 hours. Paths are relative to the config's project. A shard with rest takes every file in that folder that no other shard on the same project names, and rest of "" takes every folder no rest shard on the project takes, so a new file always lands in some shard; a config's own exclusions apply to all its shards. Core's Redaction/** is not mutated at all (core.json leaves it out): redaction is best-effort defence in depth, and the boundary is auth. Sessions/PartGate.cs is security-core's, so it is mutated once, under that config. Sized from mutant counts: keep a shard near 650.
